newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stock markets rampant in post-budget glow.
newsitem.headline: Indian stock markets rampant in post-budget glow.

text.p: Indian share prices rocketed on Monday, with the Bombay Stock Exchange top-30 index reaching an eight-month high on favourable reaction to the government's pro-growth, pro-investment budget.
The index later fell on profit-taking but setbacks were likely to be temporary, dealers said.
The breadth and focus of Finance Minister P. Chidambaram's budget, handed down last Friday, boosted confidence in India and sent investors on a buying spree, traders said.
Profit-taking in early trade knocked the BSE index off its 4,007.91 peak, the highest since June 17 last year.
The BSE index's all-time high was struck on September 12, 1994 at 4,643.
At the close, the BSE index was at a provisional 3,870.34 at 1000 GMT, up 12.85 points from Saturday's finish.
The National Stock Exchange top-50 share index was up 4.20 points to 1,107.15.
Combined with the gains made in two special post budget trading sessions on Friday evening and Saturday, the BSE index has soared about 10 percent since Chidambaram ignited buying passion.
Dealers said foreign investors were queuing up to buy into Indian shares, and the market advance has more mileage left.

"Essentially, we expect more money to come into India. There are a lot of foreign investors interested but they face difficulties sourcing stocks. Local institutions, who are the only main suppliers, are not ready to sell," Alok Sethi, director of NatWest Markets told Reuters.
Serious investors were waiting to pounce on dips, Sethi said.
"Foreign funds will go in for large market-capitalised stocks. Having missed the rally, they must be frustrated." Ajit Dayal, director at Quantum Financial Services, said.
Large market capitalised banking, and petrochemical sector stocks will draw heavy buying interest, he added.
Dayal said the BSE index would hit 4,500 points within three months.
But dealers warned a rise that was too fast could invite a stronger backlash by profit-takers.
A buying frenzy established India as the top performing market in Asia in January after hitting a three-year low in December of 2,713.12.

But scepticism about Chidamabaram's ability to deliver needed reforms, given the political constraints of working in a minority 15-party coalition government, cut deep into the rises made during the build up to the February 28 budget.
Those who kept faith had been richly rewarded and the sceptics were paying the penalty, dealers said.
"Anyone who doubted that reforms were on the stumbling block are now silent. The coalition has given us a fantastic budget," Quantum's Dayal said.

Vallabh Bhansali, director at brokers Enam Financial Consultants, saw the market heading up another 200-300 points. He was positive on the pharmaceutical, services and consumer sector, and expected interest in cyclical stocks, such as cement and aluminium.
"This is a time when everything is right for India," Dayal said.
